historical_references.context: Hubaib ibn Mundhir was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, known for his courage and determination. He participated in the Battle of Uhud (625 CE), where he led a contingent of 300 men. Despite being vastly outnumbered by the enemy, Hubaib refused to retreat, and he was one of only a few Muslims who managed to hold their ground against the advancing Sassanid Persian army.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat al-Kubra, vol. 2, p. 315 The name Hubaibi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Hubaib ibn Mundhir was also a prominent leader among the Ansar (helpers) of Medina, who welcomed and supported the Prophet Muhammad and his companions after their migration from Mecca. Hubaib played a crucial role in the defense of Medina during the early years of Islam, and he was particularly noted for his bravery and generosity.
